clue.text: Piece of bread: a man needs one at half-time

parts.note: a chap is a man
A stands for one, as in 'a pound'

indicators.note: half of the word time is taken, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A footballer wants a snack of bread at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the football interval, but it means half of the word 'time', giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an Indian flatbread, so it is a type of bread.

clue.text: Nearly grip a shellfish

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a clamp is a tool for gripping, and to clamp is to grip

explanation.surface: Someone almost grabs hold of a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts the last letter, P, from CLAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc, a familiar example of shellfish.

clue.text: It's horrific to find this sign of a meddler's share

definitions.meaning: read literally, a severed digit baked into a pastry would be a gruesome discovery
the idiom for having a hand in something, the mark of someone who involves themselves in others' affairs

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal, the second the idiom for being involved in something.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who has an interest or involvement in an affair, as a meddler does.

clue.text: Spies needing information held by ATS

indicators.note: held by means one piece is gripped inside the letters of another

parts.note: taken as written: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army corps
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Spies rely on intelligence gathered by the women's army corps.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information; the ATS was the wartime British women's army.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents are operatives working for intelligence services, that is, spies.

clue.text: Piece of office equipment, one not known to have protection

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NK is an abbreviation for not known
a pad is padding worn for protection, as by a cricketer

explanation.surface: An unidentified piece of office kit needs a protective covering.
explanation.definitionFit: An ink pad is a stamp pad found on office desks, so it is office equipment.

clue.text: Chief enemy in vault with iron ring inside

parts.note: an arch is a vaulted structure, a vault

indicators.note: inside means the ring sits within the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A villain lurks in a vaulted cellar with an iron ring set in the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An archfoe is a principal adversary, the chief of one's enemies.

clue.text: The failure did not get this

definitions.text: The failure did not get this

parts.words: The failure did not get this
parts.note: the phrase used of a flop is that it made no progress at all, and the clue asks for the last word of that phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails is said not to get to any place at all, the idiom for making no progress.

clue.text: Frozen sweets: options about a hundred

indicators.note: about means the word for options is wrapped round the letter

parts.note: choices are options
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A shopper picks among frozen treats, with about a hundred on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc-ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc-ices are bars of ice cream coated in chocolate, frozen confections.

clue.text: Original place to attract resident naval officer

parts.note: first means original, earliest
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant is a resident of a property

explanation.surface: A new home is advertised to draw a resident naval officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A first lieutenant is a rank of officer in the navy, second in command of a ship.

clue.text: I rested, having tea break in this holiday season

indicators.note: break means the letters are broken up and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rested and took a tea break during the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a tea break but signals the anagram of I RESTED plus TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastertide is the period around Easter, a season of holidays.

clue.text: A camp whisper

parts.note: a side is a faction or camp in a dispute

explanation.surface: A theatrical, camp murmur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' suggests flamboyance, but it means a side or faction.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark spoken quietly so others do not hear, a whispered comment.

clue.text: Clues about the committee, which typists know well

indicators.note: about means the word for clues goes around the word for committee

parts.note: keys are clues that unlock answers
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Hints are given about a committee that office typists are familiar with.
explanation.definitionFit: Typists work at keyboards all day, so these are what they know well.

clue.text: Novelist has a stage hit: 'A Rich Model'

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A writer's play becomes a hit with a title 'A Rich Model'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' at the end seems part of a title, but it signals the anagram of A STAGE HIT A RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was a British writer of detective novels, a novelist.

clue.text: Bachelor travels with male help for female attendant

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree
rides means travels
aid means help

explanation.surface: A single man travels with a manservant to help a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid is a woman who attends the bride at a wedding.

clue.text: It's bloody unusual

definitions.meaning: describing meat cooked so lightly that it is still red inside

explanation.surface: Something is extraordinarily strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' looks like an intensifier but describes underdone steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means both undercooked with red juices and uncommon.

clue.text: This incentive to buy is not bound to get bent

parts.note: free means not tied or bound
a bent is a natural talent, a gift

explanation.surface: A marketing bonus is never guaranteed to be crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like crooked, but means a talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A free gift is an item given away to tempt customers into buying.

clue.text: Where money is easily obtained from the wild rodeo lad

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A rodeo cowboy has found his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' signals the anagram of RODEO LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold, so it is a place of easy riches.

clue.text: Rest in part of London about one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the London district wraps around the numeral

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a lack of activity, a state of rest.

clue.text: Start the day fishing, which is swinging

indicators.note: start means only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler starts the day fishing on a swinging line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangling means hanging loosely and swaying, that is, swinging.

clue.text: Kitty is joking with small daughter

parts.note: said in fun means joking
D is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: Someone's cat plays with a little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is not a cat here but a shared pool of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money collected for a purpose, a fund.

clue.text: This record is available

definitions.meaning: a recording released as one track

explanation.definitionFit: Single names both a one-track record release and a person free to date.

clue.text: Value today's muck

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, today's dating
mire is mud or muck

explanation.surface: Someone prizes the dirt of the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: To value someone or something is to hold them in high regard, to admire them.

clue.text: Learners reshaping horn with cold chisel

indicators.note: reshaping means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Craft students shape a horn using a cold chisel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshaping' signals the anagram of HORN and COLD CHISEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren are pupils, people learning at school.

clue.text: Put up with beard being trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates their beard being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Calling for a parish priest before joining type of comedy

indicators.note: before means the priest's letters come ahead of what follows

parts.note: Ealing comedies were films from London's Ealing Studios

explanation.surface: A vicar gets ready to join a comedy troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing comedies were classic British film comedies made at Ealing Studios in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means making an earnest request, calling for something.

clue.text: Portrait that is on the outside of a magazine

indicators.note: on the outside of means the abbreviation surrounds the other piece

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A portrait appears on the cover of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness, such as a portrait.

clue.text: Fade away, being disheartened after endless diet

indicators.note: after means the word for disheartened follows the shortened word
endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A dieter fades away, dispirited by a never-ending regime.
explanation.definitionFit: To die down is to subside or fade gradually.

clue.text: Constituent of carrot/celery blend making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the run of letters is read backwards
the run of letters is blended into the words carrot and celery, held within them

explanation.surface: An ingredient of a vegetable blend comes back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading carroT/CELEry backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a voter in a constituency, an elector.
